D4_canonicalConstructionBoundary.question: What is the canonical construction boundary for record field sets?
rule: INCLUDE transforms chained inside the declaration expression itself (e.g. `const x = [...].map(...)`). These are part of how the source defines the value.
EXCLUDE fields added by separate statements executed after the declaration (e.g. `x.forEach(r => { r.f = ... })`). These are derived runtime enrichment, not declared semantics.

evidence.worked_example: systemRecords is declared as `[...].map(record => ({...record, description: 'Governed Universe system entity; ...'}))`, so description is declared. domainIds is added later by `systemRecords.forEach(record => { record.domainIds = ... })`, so domainIds is derived, not declared.

D4_canonicalConstructionBoundary.fabricationCheck: No field is invented or dropped by assumption; the rule is decided by where the source itself places the assignment.

D5_fieldSetDivergence.question: What causes the 189 field-set-divergent records?

breakdown.cause: R0.1A captured the pre-chain array literal instead of the full declaration expression, so the declared `description` field is missing from businessObjectRecords.
Same pre-chain capture defect on systemRecords.
Two different entity types share an id string; the R0.1A consistency detector keys only on id across heterogeneous record sets.

D5_fieldSetDivergence.impact: Two certified structures understate their declared field set. Under D4 they should carry `description` and should not carry `domainIds`. No Universe semantics are lost from the source; the source remains intact and re-extractable.
D5_fieldSetDivergence.remediation: A corrected mechanical re-materialization capturing the full declaration expression. This is a re-run of R0.1A extraction under a corrected boundary rule and must be authorized as such; R0.1B does not rewrite the payload.
D5_fieldSetDivergence.reportedUnder: CLAUDE.md rule permitting a closed stage to be revisited only when a new governed defect is found and reported.

D6_stateClassification.question: Does materialized `state` belong in the canonical semantic payload?
D6_stateClassification.evidence: `state` is produced by `bindStateAliases(createCanonicalState())`, and createCanonicalState returns navigationState (family, selection, selectedEntityId) and activeContext (mode, role, movementPatternId, nodeId, jurisdictionId, ...). These are user-interface selection values, not Universe ontology.
D6_stateClassification.remediation: Exclude `state` from the canonical semantic payload and record it as RUNTIME_UI_STATE in the declaration inventory. Applied during the D5 remediation, not by R0.1B.
